dram-001.question: Which correctly describes the structure of a typical 1-bit DRAM memory cell?
choices: One transistor with a floating gate
dram-001.explanation: A DRAM cell consists of one transistor and one capacitor (1T1C) and stores one bit according to whether the capacitor is charged. Six transistors is the SRAM cell, and a floating-gate transistor is the flash memory cell.

dram-002.question: Why does DRAM need periodic refresh operations?
choices: Because the number of writes is limited
Because the charge stored in the capacitor is gradually lost through leakage current
dram-002.explanation: The charge stored in a DRAM capacitor is gradually lost through leakage currents in the transistor and junctions. Refresh reads and rewrites the data at regular intervals (generally within tens of milliseconds) before it is lost. A limited number of writes is a characteristic of flash memory.

dram-003.question: Which correctly describes the read operation of DRAM?
choices: Reading does not change the cell's charge at all
Reading changes the cell's charge, so the data is amplified by a sense amplifier and written back to the cell
Reading uses tunneling current at high voltage
dram-003.explanation: In DRAM, connecting the cell capacitor to the bit line shares its charge with the bit line, destroying the original state (destructive read). The sense amplifier therefore amplifies the tiny voltage difference to determine the data and at the same time writes the amplified value back to the cell.

dram-004.question: Which pair of three-dimensional structures has been used in DRAM cells to secure capacitor capacitance?
dram-004.explanation: To secure enough capacitance as cells shrink, DRAM capacitors have been made three-dimensional. There are trench capacitors, formed by etching deep holes into the substrate, and stacked capacitors, built as tall structures above the transistor; stacked capacitors are now mainstream. Floating gate and charge trap are flash memory structures.

dram-005.question: Which correctly describes a property of DRAM?
choices: It is volatile memory that loses data when the power is turned off
It is non-volatile memory that retains data when the power is turned off
It is read-only memory that cannot be rewritten
dram-005.explanation: DRAM stores information as charge on a capacitor and is volatile: when power is turned off, the charge is not maintained and the data is lost. Even with power on, the charge gradually leaks away, so refresh is needed. Non-volatile memories such as flash retain data without power.

dram-006.question: What does 'DDR (double data rate)' in DDR SDRAM mean?
choices: Data is transferred on both the rising and falling edges of the clock
It operates at twice the supply voltage
dram-006.explanation: DDR transfers data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock, achieving twice the data rate at the same clock frequency. With each generation (DDR2, DDR3, DDR4, DDR5), transfer rates have increased and supply voltages have decreased.

dram-007.question: In a DRAM cell array, which line connects to the gates of the cell transistors and selects the row to be read or written?
dram-007.explanation: In a DRAM cell array, the word line selects a row and turns on the cell transistors, and the capacitor charge is read or written through the bit line. The bit line leads to a sense amplifier.

dram-008.question: How does the data retention time of DRAM cells generally change as temperature rises?
dram-008.explanation: As temperature rises, junction leakage current increases and the capacitor charge is lost faster, so retention time gets shorter. For this reason, DRAM standards include provisions for shortening the refresh interval at high temperatures.

dram-009.question: Which correctly describes a soft error in memory?
choices: An error in which stored data is temporarily flipped by radiation or the like, without damaging the device
A permanent failure due to a wiring defect during manufacturing
A failure in which the device breaks down due to aging
dram-009.explanation: A soft error occurs when alpha particles from package materials or neutrons originating from cosmic rays generate charge in silicon and flip stored data. The device itself is not damaged, so rewriting the data restores normal operation. Error-correcting codes (ECC) and similar measures are used.

dram-010.question: Compared with SRAM, which is a characteristic of DRAM?
choices: It is faster than SRAM and needs no refresh
Its cells are small and the cost per bit is low, but it needs refresh
It retains data when the power is turned off
dram-010.explanation: DRAM is made of small 1T1C cells, so it is easier to make in large capacities than 6T SRAM and has a lower cost per bit. On the other hand, it needs refresh and is slower than SRAM, so DRAM is used for main memory and SRAM for caches.

dram-011.question: Which correctly describes redundancy repair, used to improve DRAM yield?
choices: Rows or columns containing defective cells are replaced with spare rows or columns prepared in advance
All chips containing defective cells are discarded
The supply voltage is raised to make defective cells work
dram-011.explanation: In large-capacity memory such as DRAM, discarding a whole chip because of a few defective cells would greatly reduce yield. Spare rows and columns are therefore provided, and defective locations found in testing are switched to spares using fuses or similar means.

dram-012.question: What does an error-correcting code (ECC) used in memory do?
choices: Adds redundant bits to data to detect and correct bit errors
dram-012.explanation: ECC adds check bits to data so that errors can be detected and corrected when the data is read. To reduce the impact of soft errors and defects due to scaling, ECC is used in server memory, and DDR5 also builds ECC into the chip itself.

dram-013.question: In DRAM, why is access time shorter when the same row (page) is accessed repeatedly?
choices: Because refresh is no longer needed
Because the data of an activated row is held in the sense amplifiers and can be read by just switching columns
dram-013.explanation: In DRAM, activating a row reads the data of all cells in that row into the sense amplifiers. Data in the same row can be read just by changing the column address without reactivating the row, so access is faster. Memory controllers use this property to optimize the order of accesses.

dram-014.question: Why are high-k materials such as zirconium oxide used for the dielectric film of DRAM capacitors?
choices: To secure the necessary capacitance in a small area
To make the capacitor emit light
dram-014.explanation: Capacitance is proportional to permittivity. Even as cells shrink, a certain capacitance is needed to read data correctly, so high-k materials such as ZrO2, with higher permittivity than SiO2, are used to obtain the needed capacitance in a small area.

dram-015.question: Which correctly describes the self-refresh mode of DRAM?
choices: A mode that erases all data
A mode in which the DRAM refreshes itself internally without external commands, retaining data at low power, for example during standby
A mode that doubles access speed
dram-015.explanation: In self-refresh mode, the DRAM refreshes itself using an internal timer. Because no commands are needed from the memory controller, data can be retained at low power, for example while a smartphone or PC is asleep.

dram-016.question: How much is an 8 Gbit DRAM chip in bytes?
dram-016.explanation: One byte is 8 bits, so 8 Gbit ÷ 8 = 1 GB. Memory chip capacity is usually given in bits, while memory module capacity is usually given in bytes. For example, eight 8 Gbit chips make an 8 GB module.

dram-017.question: What does the CAS latency (CL) of DRAM mean?
choices: The number of clock cycles from a read command (specifying the column address) until data is output
The supply voltage of the DRAM
dram-017.explanation: CAS latency is the number of clock cycles from receiving a read command that specifies the column address until the first data is output. A smaller value means a faster response, but the actual time is the product with the clock period, so faster-clocked standards have larger CL numbers.

dram-018.question: What is the main use of the DRAM standard called LPDDR?
choices: Devices that require low power, such as smartphones
dram-018.explanation: LPDDR (low-power DDR) is a mobile DRAM standard that reduces power with lower supply voltages, power-saving modes and other features. It is used in smartphones, tablets and thin laptops, and is sometimes stacked in the same package as the processor.

dram-019.question: Which is a characteristic of GDDR, used as graphics memory for GPUs?
choices: It is a standard that emphasizes data transfer bandwidth (speed)
It retains data when the power is turned off
It is slow but very cheap
dram-019.explanation: GDDR is a DRAM standard that emphasizes data transfer speed so that GPUs can handle large amounts of image data quickly. Its per-pin data rate is higher than ordinary DDR, and it is used in graphics cards and game consoles. When even more bandwidth is needed, HBM is used.

dram-020.question: What is the main purpose of burying the gate electrode in a trench in the silicon substrate (buried word line) in recent DRAM cell transistors?
choices: To make the cell emit light
To lengthen the effective channel and suppress leakage while shrinking the cell
To eliminate the need for a capacitor
dram-020.explanation: DRAM cell transistors need extremely low leakage so that the capacitor charge does not escape. Burying the gate in a trench allows a longer effective channel along the trench even with small planar dimensions, suppressing leakage due to short-channel effects.

dram-021.question: In DRAM, what is the main reason for splitting the address into row and column addresses and supplying them in turn through the same pins?
choices: To reduce the number of address pins
To eliminate the need for refresh
dram-021.explanation: DRAM has a large capacity, so supplying the whole address at once would require many pins. Supplying the row and column addresses through the same pins at different times (address multiplexing) reduces the number of pins. It also matches DRAM's internal operation of activating a row and then selecting a column.

dram-022.question: What is the main purpose of dividing the inside of a DRAM into multiple banks?
choices: To overlap operations in different banks and improve effective access performance
dram-022.explanation: Activating and precharging a DRAM row takes time. With multiple banks, one bank can be accessed while another performs these operations, hiding the wait time and improving overall transfer efficiency.

dram-023.question: Why is the voltage change on the bit line very small when DRAM is read?
choices: Because the supply voltage is very high
Because the bit line resistance is zero
Because the cell capacitor's capacitance is much smaller than the bit line's parasitic capacitance
dram-023.explanation: During a read, the cell capacitor's charge is shared with the bit line. The cell capacitance is much smaller than the bit line capacitance, so the bit line voltage changes only slightly (tens to around a hundred-odd mV). The sense amplifier amplifies this small change to decide 0 or 1.

dram-024.question: Which correctly describes the idea of 3D DRAM, under research and development as a way to increase future DRAM capacity?
choices: Stacking memory cells vertically to increase capacity without relying only on planar scaling
Increasing capacity just by making the chip larger
dram-024.explanation: Planar scaling of DRAM is becoming difficult, so 3D DRAM, which stacks memory cells vertically like 3D NAND, is under research and development. Structures that lay the capacitors and transistors horizontally and stack them are being considered.

dram-025.question: In DRAM, what is the phenomenon in which repeatedly activating one row in a short time can flip data in adjacent rows?
dram-025.explanation: Row hammer is a phenomenon in which repeatedly activating the word line of one row makes cells in adjacent rows lose charge more easily, flipping their data. It became apparent as scaling brought cells closer together and also became a security issue. Countermeasures include extra refreshes for rows next to frequently accessed ones.

dram-026.question: Which correctly describes the main leakage paths that determine the data retention time of DRAM cells?
choices: Subthreshold leakage of the cell transistor and junction leakage
dram-026.explanation: The charge on a DRAM capacitor is lost mainly through subthreshold leakage when the cell transistor is off and through leakage at the storage-node junction (including GIDL). Reducing these extends retention time and lowers refresh frequency and power.

dram-027.question: What does F mean in '6F²', used to express DRAM cell area?
dram-027.explanation: F represents the minimum feature size, and cell area is expressed as a multiple of F squared. 6F² means an area six times the square of the minimum feature size. DRAM cell structures have improved from 8F² to 6F², and research aims to achieve 4F².

dram-028.question: In DRAM access, what is the operation called that closes the open row and returns the bit lines to an intermediate voltage to prepare for activating the next row?
dram-028.explanation: Before accessing a different row, DRAM must precharge: close the current row and return the bit lines to an intermediate voltage. This time is included in access latency, so its impact is reduced by increasing consecutive accesses to the same row and by using multiple banks.

dram-029.question: Which function, adopted in DDR5, corrects errors inside the DRAM chip?
dram-029.explanation: To cope with more cell defects and errors due to scaling, DDR5 builds an error-correction circuit into the DRAM chip itself (on-die ECC). Separate from system-level ECC, it corrects single-bit errors and similar errors inside the chip.

dram-030.question: What is the performance limitation called that arises because improvements in memory bandwidth and latency have not kept up with improvements in processor performance?
dram-030.explanation: Processor computing performance has improved greatly, but DRAM access latency and bandwidth have not improved as much, so time spent waiting for data has come to limit performance. This is called the memory wall. Larger caches and high-bandwidth memories such as HBM are responses to it.

dram-031.question: What does "RAM (random access memory)" in DRAM mean?
choices: Read-only memory that cannot be rewritten
Memory in which any address can be read or written directly in roughly the same time
Memory that can only be read sequentially from the beginning
dram-031.explanation: Random access means that by specifying an address, any location can be accessed directly regardless of order. It contrasts with sequential access, where you must go through the data in order, as with magnetic tape. Read-only memory is called ROM.
choiceNotes: Read-only memory is ROM.
Correct. Any address can be accessed directly.
Memory that can only be read in order is sequential-access memory.

dram-032.question: In PCs and servers, what is DRAM mainly used for?
choices: Long-term storage that retains data after power-off
Main memory that holds running programs and their data
dram-032.explanation: DRAM offers large capacity at relatively high speed, so it is used as main memory holding the programs and data the CPU is running. Because it is volatile and loses data when power is removed, SSDs and HDDs are used for long-term storage. Registers and caches inside the CPU use SRAM and flip-flops.
choiceNotes: DRAM is volatile and loses data at power-off, so it is unsuited to long-term storage.
CPU registers are built from flip-flops and similar circuits.
Correct. DRAM is used as main memory.

dram-033.question: What is the component called in which several DRAM chips are mounted on a small board that plugs into a PC as memory?
dram-033.explanation: A DIMM (dual inline memory module) is a memory module with several DRAM chips mounted on one board, used by plugging it into a slot on the motherboard. The smaller version for laptops is called an SO-DIMM.
choiceNotes: Correct. It is a memory module carrying DRAM chips.
An SSD is a storage device that uses flash memory.
The motherboard is the main board into which the CPU and memory are plugged.

dram-034.question: What does the "S" (synchronous) in SDRAM indicate?
choices: It operates in sync with an external clock signal
It has the same cell structure as SRAM
dram-034.explanation: SDRAM is DRAM that accepts commands and transfers data in sync with a clock signal. Synchronization enabled pipelining and burst transfers, making it faster. DDR SDRAM developed this idea further.
choiceNotes: SDRAM is also volatile and loses data at power-off.
Correct. It is DRAM that operates in sync with a clock.
SDRAM cells use the same 1T1C structure as ordinary DRAM.

dram-035.question: Which trio correctly names the three major manufacturers holding large shares of the global DRAM market?
dram-035.explanation: The DRAM market is an oligopoly dominated by Samsung Electronics and SK hynix of South Korea and Micron Technology of the United States. Intel, AMD and NVIDIA are processor and GPU companies, and TSMC, GlobalFoundries and UMC are foundries.
choiceNotes: Intel, AMD and NVIDIA are mainly processor and GPU companies.
TSMC, GlobalFoundries and UMC are contract-manufacturing foundries.
Correct. These three hold most of the DRAM market.

dram-036.question: In typical DRAM standards, which is closest to the period within which every cell must be refreshed once? (Normal temperature range)
dram-036.explanation: Typical DDR-family DRAMs require all rows to be refreshed within about 64 ms in the normal temperature range. In practice, refresh commands are issued several thousand times within this period, refreshing a few rows at a time.
choiceNotes: Correct. All cells are normally refreshed within 64 ms.
64 µs is too short; refresh would take up too much time.
64 s is too long for cells to retain their data.

dram-037.question: What does the DRAM timing parameter tRCD represent?
choices: The time from closing a row until the next row can be opened
The time from activating a row until it can be read or written using a column address
dram-037.explanation: tRCD (RAS to CAS delay) is the time required after an activate command opens a row before read or write commands can be issued to that row. The time from closing a row to opening the next is tRP (precharge time).
choiceNotes: The time from closing a row to opening the next is tRP.
Correct. It is the time from row activation to column access.
The refresh period is specified by parameters such as tREFI.

dram-038.question: Which correctly describes a DRAM burst transfer?
choices: A single read command transfers several consecutive data words, one after another on successive clocks
Refresh and data transfer are performed at the same time
dram-038.explanation: In a burst transfer, one read or write command transfers several data words at consecutive addresses (for example, 8) on successive clocks. Because a command is not needed for each word, blocks of data such as cache lines can be transferred efficiently.
choiceNotes: Correct. One command transfers consecutive data together.
DRAM burst transfer does not compress data.
Normal reads and writes cannot be performed during refresh.

dram-039.question: Which is closest to the peak bandwidth of one channel of DDR4 memory with a data rate of 3,200 MT/s and a 64-bit data bus?
dram-039.explanation: Peak bandwidth is the transfer rate times the bus width. 3,200 × 10⁶ transfers/s × 64 bits = 3,200 × 10⁶ × 8 bytes = 25.6 × 10⁹ bytes/s, or about 25.6 GB/s.
choiceNotes: About 3.2 GB/s would correspond to an 8-bit (1-byte) bus.
About 204.8 GB/s results from mixing up bits and bytes.
Correct. 3,200 MT/s × 8 bytes = 25.6 GB/s.

dram-040.question: What is the main effect of running PC memory in dual-channel mode?
choices: Two memory channels are used simultaneously, roughly doubling peak bandwidth
dram-040.explanation: In dual-channel mode, the memory controller transfers data over two independent channels at the same time, roughly doubling peak bandwidth. Capacity is set by the total of the modules and is independent of the number of channels. Latency hardly changes.
choiceNotes: Capacity is the total of the installed modules and is not doubled by channels.
Correct. Two channels in parallel roughly double the bandwidth.
The latency of a single access hardly changes.

dram-041.question: Which correctly describes a "rank" on a DRAM module?
choices: A performance grade of DRAM chips
The number of banks inside one chip
A group of DRAM chips accessed together to make up the full data bus width (for example, 64 bits)
dram-041.explanation: A rank is a group of DRAM chips selected together by a chip-select signal that collectively make up the full width of the data bus. For example, eight 8-bit-wide (x8) chips form one 64-bit rank. Putting multiple ranks on one module increases capacity.
choiceNotes: Rank does not denote a performance grade.
The internal divisions of a chip are called banks.
Correct. It is the group of chips forming the full data bus width.

dram-042.question: How many 8-bit-wide (x8) DRAM chips are needed per rank to form a 64-bit data bus (without ECC)?
dram-042.explanation: 64 bits ÷ 8 bits = 8, so eight x8 chips accessed together form a 64-bit-wide bus. Modules with ECC typically add one more chip (nine in total) for the check bits.
choiceNotes: Correct. 64 ÷ 8 = 8 chips.
Four chips would give only a 32-bit width.
64 chips would be needed with 1-bit-wide (x1) chips.

dram-043.question: In most current PC processors, where is the memory controller that controls DRAM located?
dram-043.explanation: The memory controller, once located in the chipset (northbridge) on the motherboard, is now generally integrated into the processor. This shortens the path between CPU and memory and reduces latency.
choiceNotes: DRAM chips follow commands sent by an external memory controller.
Correct. It is now generally integrated into the processor.
An SSD controller manages flash memory and does not control DRAM main memory.

dram-044.question: What is commonly required by DRAM standards when the chip temperature is in the high range (for example, above 85 °C)?
choices: Refresh more often (shorten the refresh interval)
dram-044.explanation: At high temperatures, junction leakage in the cells increases and the data retention time shortens. Many DRAM standards therefore require more frequent refresh in the high-temperature range, for example by halving the refresh interval.
choiceNotes: Stopping refresh would lose data.
Raising the clock frequency does not solve the retention problem.
Correct. Retention time is shorter at high temperatures, so refresh is done more often.

dram-045.question: As DRAM capacity grows, what tends to become a problem with respect to refresh?
choices: More rows must be refreshed, so a larger share of time and power goes to refresh
The refresh period must be lengthened
dram-045.explanation: As capacity increases, more cells must be refreshed within the same time. This increases both the time during which normal access is unavailable and the power spent on refresh, affecting performance and power consumption. Techniques such as per-bank refresh have been introduced to mitigate this.
choiceNotes: As long as it is DRAM, refresh is required.
Correct. The refresh burden increases.
Retention time does not get longer with capacity, so the period does not need to lengthen.

dram-046.question: In DRAM cell arrays, which bit-line arrangement places the paired bit lines side by side within the same array?
dram-046.explanation: In the folded bit-line architecture, the pair of bit lines connected to a sense amplifier runs side by side in the same array, so noise couples equally onto both and is easily cancelled differentially. The open bit-line architecture, which places the paired lines in separate arrays on either side, is more noise-sensitive but allows a smaller cell area (such as 6F²).
choiceNotes: The open bit-line architecture places the paired lines in separate arrays on either side of the sense amplifier.
Correct. The paired bit lines run side by side in the same array.
A divided word line is not a bit-line pairing arrangement.

dram-047.question: Which correctly describes the idea of "8n prefetch" used in memories such as DDR4 SDRAM?
choices: Data eight times the I/O width is fetched from the internal array at once and output in sequence at high speed through the external pins
Eight refresh operations are performed together
The same data is written to eight chips
dram-047.explanation: Because the DRAM cell array itself cannot run much faster, the device internally reads eight times the I/O width (8n) in a single access and sends it out in sequence over the fast external interface. This raises the external transfer rate without speeding up the internal array.
choiceNotes: Correct. Wide data is read internally and output quickly externally.
It is not a mechanism for grouping refreshes.
It is not a mechanism for writing the same data to several chips.

dram-048.question: In DDR-family DRAM, which feature places termination resistors inside the DRAM chip, with controllable on/off, to suppress signal reflections?
dram-048.explanation: At high signal speeds, reflections at the end of a line distort the waveform. ODT places termination resistors inside the DRAM chip and enables them only when needed. It reduces components on the board while maintaining good signal quality even on buses shared by several modules.
choiceNotes: ECC corrects errors and is unrelated to termination.
Self-refresh lets the DRAM refresh itself while idle.
Correct. It is on-chip termination.

dram-049.question: Some DRAM cells have a data retention time that irregularly switches between longer and shorter values over time. What is this phenomenon called?
dram-049.explanation: VRT (variable retention time) is a phenomenon in which a cell's leakage current switches due to changes in the state of a defect, so its retention time hops irregularly between two or more values. A cell that appears to have sufficient retention during testing may later get shorter, so margin is needed in refresh design and testing.
choiceNotes: Row hammer is data flipping caused by frequently activating an adjacent row.
Correct. It is the irregular fluctuation of retention time.
A soft error is a temporary data flip caused by radiation or similar.

dram-050.question: Why is a boosted voltage (VPP), higher than the supply voltage, used to drive DRAM word lines?
choices: To avoid losing a threshold voltage across the cell transistor so the capacitor is written with a full voltage
dram-050.explanation: The cell transistor is an nMOS device, so if its gate were driven only to the supply voltage, the capacitor could be written only to a voltage one threshold voltage lower. Driving the word line with VPP, at least a threshold voltage above the supply, writes a full "1" voltage to the capacitor and secures read margin.
choiceNotes: Correct. It avoids the threshold voltage drop.
It is not meant to lower the bit-line voltage.
Refresh is still required even with boosting.
